about: Every tool under tools/: its category (the folder it lives in), the question it answers, how it is run and its tests. An instrument carries a real output sample from this machine and how to read it; tools/README.md is written from this file by tools/checks/check-catalog.mjs --write, and check:boundaries holds the two to each other and to the tree.

tools.question: Does a title run in a browser, and what did the run do?
tools.sample:
The Swapper undefined -- TheSwapper.exe
  ran for 13ms, 4 guest instructions
stopped: exited with 3221225477
errors -- what the engine did not do:
  mscoree.dll!_CorExeMain: not implemented, answered with nothing
1 imports nothing claimed:
  mscoree.dll  (1)
tools.source: tools/cdp_test/reports/game-2026-11-14T03-28-29-645Z.txt (a run of steam-231160 without its .NET runtime; it printed "undefined" for the missing version, which the title line now leaves out)
tools.read: The first lines are how the run ended (exit 0xC0000005 here); "errors" and "imports nothing claimed" are what the engine lacked, the first thing to implement. The rest of a report is the address space, the last host calls and, with flags, profiles and frames.

tools.question: What does a frame cost once a title is up, and where does the time go?
Did a title get worse: does it still reach its game, and do its frames come as evenly as before?
tools.command: node tools/run/smoke.mjs <bundle-id> [--runs 3] [--against FILE]; on runs already made: smoke.mjs span <presents.json> | drops <frames.json>...

tools.question: What does the launcher's own page cost while a title runs?
tools.command: node tools/run/launcher.mjs <bundle-id> (launcher running: npm run ui)

tools.question: Does the launcher lay out on a phone, a tablet and a desktop?
Where does an installer, or an installed program, stop in Node, and what is each process waiting on?
tools.command: node tools/run/install-watch.mjs <setup.exe | disc.iso | archive.zip> | --bundle ID [--which PATH] [--args ARGS]
tools.read: Each line is seconds since the start and what happened: OUT is what the program printed, divergence a call answered otherwise than Windows would, then how each process ended. Here Wine's stateblock test ran 9283 checks and one failed (render state 0x9b read back 1.0, expected 0).

tools.question: Play a bottle from this checkout, with nothing else set up
tools.command: node tools/run/play.mjs <bundle-id> (then open the page it prints)

tools.question: Do Wine's conformance tests pass in the engine?
tools.sample:
winetest build 4e819f054dd2d9ee855ee3f1e30d8c1bb8f80fcf, 2 at a time, 120 s each
  kernel32:sync                pass            executed 355430 failures     0   11.7 s
tools.read: One row a test: how it ended, the checks it executed and those that failed, and its time; report.md beside it groups the failing lines and, with --baseline, says what got worse.

tools.question: Where do the Visual C++ runtimes' own load checks let a program run, against Windows?
tools.sample:
ok   vc80-crt: external program.manifest; the runtime and its manifest beside the program -- Windows runs, engine runs
ok   vc80-crt: LoadLibrary, embedded manifest; the runtime and its manifest beside it -- Windows runs, engine runs
ok   vc80-crt: the runtime installed: only in system32, the store presents it -- Windows runs (as with the redistribut
ok   vc80-crt: no manifest at all; the runtime beside the program -- Windows R6034, engine runs
ok   vc80-crt: LoadLibrary, no manifest at all; the runtime beside the program -- Windows R6034, engine runs
tools.read: A row a runtime and a deployment layout: what Windows does and what the engine did; DIFF marks a row where they part, "by decision" one the engine answers itself on purpose.

tools.question: What does a phone's browser keep, and which wasm tail call takes its page down?
tools.command: open tools/run/webkit-probe/tail-calls.html or storage.html from the launcher on the phone

tools.question: What is a game a person plays doing right now: console, phases, profile, memory, picture, sound?
tools.sample:
21757 ms sampled: idle   6.1%, garbage collection   2.9%
self:
   35.0%  sleep engine.worker.js:12892
   13.6%  waitWhile engine.worker.js:12882
    8.1%  showNow engine.worker.js:450658
inclusive:
  100.0%  (root) :0
   67.8%  run engine.worker.js:837745
^showNow : 2004 of 21757 ms (9.2%)
    9.2%  show engine.worker.js:450858  <  presentTo engine.worker.js:835602  <  present engine.worker.js:82812
tools.read: Attached commands need the shared browser; profile --file and diff read files. Self time is the function itself, inclusive with what it called; a stretch is time outside translated code (led by sleep or waitWhile it is the thread parked, not working). --callers says who reached a function, by the time under it: showNow is 9.2 % of this engine worker, all through present.

tools.question: Where did a person's DevTools trace go, by thread and function?
tools.command: node tools/read/trace-summary.mjs <Trace-*.json.gz> (a trace the person saved)

tools.question: What do a title's real frames cost the graphics worker, played again in Node?
Does our HLSL compiler agree with Microsoft's on a title's own shaders?
tools.command: node tools/read/shader-diff.mjs <game-*-shaders dir> (from a game.mjs run; Windows for D3DCompiler)

tools.question: Where are the gaps, clicks and repeats in what the person heard?
What does a run in Node cost the translator, and where did the program stop?
tools.command: node tools/translator/launch-probe.mjs <bundle-id> [--turns N] [--series S] [--translation-store DIR] [--cork-out FILE]
tools.sample:
mode: default, 1 executor(s), cork {}; node 26.13.1, V8 14.6.202.34-node.40, branch hints read
Wine d3d8 tests -- d3d8_test.exe
  entry image: 745472 bytes
every import bound.
  [guest 2] 1008:visual: 141799 tests executed (0 marked as todo, 0 as flaky, 3168 failures), 15 skipped.
stopped: exited with 255
tools.read: The head is the mode and what was bound; then what the program printed, and "stopped:" how the run ended, followed by the calls it made last and, with --series or --cork-out, the translator's figures. Here Wine's d3d8 visual test ran in Node, where nothing is drawn, so its read-backs fail by design.

tools.question: Which guest instructions does a run execute most, what does each kind cost, and how do its calls go?
tools.sample:
114795 blocks, 5435328071 instructions in TheSwapper.exe, clr.dll@0x2dea000, 1082654156 block executions outside them
share  ops-share  ops/insn  form
  9.6%      14.1%        48  push r32
  3.3%       9.7%        95  mov m32,r32
  4.0%       7.2%        59  call rel
  4.8%       7.0%        48  jne rel
tools.read: share is of the executed instructions, ops-share of the wasm operations they cost, ops/insn what one form costs: a form whose ops-share is far above its share (push stack32, 147 ops) is where the translator spends. --calls prints the calls' shape as JSON (direct, indirect, import; registers live around them).

tools.question: What machine code, wasm text or wasm bytes does a region become, weighed by how often it ran?
tools.command: node tools/translator/cork-asm.mjs --image DLL@BASE | --bin FILE --at A --entry A [--blocks FILE] [--classes|--wat|--expansion]
tools.sample:
entry  blocks  x86  wasm B  machine  bytes  per x86  ran x86  weighted
0x00401160      43  229   11492     3297  15122    14.40       9M      2.94
ran: 0.01 G guest instructions in these blocks, 2.940 machine instructions an executed one
by kind, an executed guest instruction: other 0.935 (31.8%), branch 0.606 (20.6%), memory 0.444 (15.1%), compare 0.395
tools.read: "per x86" is machine instructions a guest instruction becomes in the code as compiled; "weighted" the same over what ran. The kinds line says where the instructions go besides the guest's own work (branch, memory, frame spills). The host here is arm64 (this VM).

tools.question: Which function of a system or runtime DLL is hot?
tools.sample:
48991 public symbols; the image 55.6% of 2436222218 block executions
  2.11%  ?mark_object_simple1@gc_heap@WKS@@KGXPAE@Z
  1.68%  ?relocate_address@gc_heap@WKS@@KGXPAPAE@Z
  1.43%  ?relocate_survivors_in_plug@gc_heap@WKS@@KGXPAE0PAUrelocate_args@12@@Z
  1.41%  ?FillEntryDataForAncestor@MethodDataObject@MethodTable@@IAEXPAV2@@Z
tools.read: The image's share of the run's block executions, then its public functions by share: here the CLR's garbage collector (mark, relocate) leads The Swapper's ngen load.

tools.question: What is the code at module+offset, as a profile names it?
tools.sample:
== clr.dll+0xb5a08
  000b5a08  8d65f4               lea      esp, [ebp - 0xc]
  000b5a0b  5f                   pop      edi
  000b5a0c  5e                   pop      esi
  000b5a0d  8b4dfc               mov      ecx, dword ptr [ebp - 4]
  000b5a10  33cd                 xor      ecx, ebp
tools.read: Offset in the module, bytes, instruction: the hottest clr.dll address of the ngen load is a function's epilogue (its security cookie check, then ret 4).

tools.question: What does one call into the host, or one maths operation, cost?
tools.sample:
N 2000000, 3 rounds; ns a call is the median over the rounds; node 26.13.1, V8 14.6.202.34-node.40, branch hints read
                                this ns/call      min..max  host calls
KERNEL32.dll!lstrlenA(s:a)                24         2..27           1
KERNEL32.dll!GetACP()                    204      190..214     2000001
tools.read: ns a call over the loop without it, the spread of the rounds, and the host calls the bridge counted: lstrlenA is guest code (1 host call, the exit), GetACP crosses every time, about 200 ns. A spread wider than the median is noise: raise N.

tools.question: Where do several executors beat one?
tools.sample:
T=2 K=- H=- E=1  best3 1.55s [1.26 1.83 1.56]  x1.00 vs E=1  1807 MIPS (2.80 G)  elsewhere 0% 0 calls
T=2 K=- H=- E=2  best3 1.01s [0.96 1.32 0.77]  x1.53 vs E=1  2762 MIPS (2.80 G)  elsewhere 53% 2 calls
best of several executors: T=2 K=- H=- E=2  x1.53
tools.read: A row a point: the mean of its three fastest runs [each run], the ratio to one executor, MIPS, and the share run elsewhere. Here two threads ran 1.53 times as fast on two executors. Runs of one point that differ threefold (an earlier run of this sweep on the loaded machine gave 7.23 against 0.78 s) are the machine, not the engine: rerun on a quiet one.

tools.question: What does a title import, or look up by name, that this build does not export?
tools.sample:
15 images read
PACKED? bundle.btl:Futuremark\3DMark03\fmod.dll: its imports are looked up at run time
NAMED, NO LIBRARY mscoree.dll  <- EasyFMSI.exe, FMSI.dll, FMSIX.dll, atimgpud.dll, cpuidsdk.dll, SI3.dll, msvcr71.dll,
NAMED, NO LIBRARY atiadlxy.dll  <- FMSI.dll
MISSING BY NAME kernel32.dll (20)
  __C_specific_handler  <- cpuidsdk.dll
  OpenProcessToken  <- mfc70.dll
tools.read: PACKED is an image whose imports are found at run time (run it to know); NAMED, NO LIBRARY a DLL its strings name that nothing provides; MISSING BY NAME a function a program may GetProcAddress that this build does not export, with who names it.

tools.question: Pack, verify, list, size, prune or extract a bottle, or unpack a zip of any size
tools.sample:
463.5 MiB   284  Futuremark\3DMark03
     2.2 MiB     7  Common Files\Futuremark Shared
     0.0 MiB     1  .bottlify\registry.json
   465.7 MiB   292  total
   0.01 GiB       1 files  3dmark11-setup.exe
   0.20 GiB       1 files  cab1.cab
tools.source: make-btl.mjs tree 3dmark03 2; make-btl.mjs zip list to_install/3dmark11/3dmark11.zip --depth=1
tools.read: tree: bytes and files under each folder to a depth, largest first, so a setup's leftovers stand out; zip list the same for an archive before unpacking it.

tools.question: Do our stdcall entries pop the bytes Windows' do?
tools.sample: 2641 stdcall entries checked, 0 pop a different number of bytes
tools.read: Every stdcall entry of the win32 layer against its Wine spec; a line per entry that pops another number of bytes, each one a caller's stack moved a call at a time. Run by hand: the specs are fetched once (import-audit --fetch-specs) and not kept in the repository.
